_readme: Suppression list for .github/workflows/npm-advisories.yml. JSON carries no comments, so the
rules live here. The gate blocks on high/critical advisories only; moderate and low are
reported and never fail a build.
TWO LISTS, ON PURPOSE.
accepted[] — a decision. Requires `reason` (>= 10 chars, what makes this tolerable HERE) and
`expires`. On the expiry date it becomes blocking again, so an acceptance is a
dated promise to revisit, never a permanent pardon. Extending one is a commit
someone reviews.
baseline   — the advisories that already existed when the gate was armed (2026-08-18),
recorded verbatim from that run. No reason is written for them because nobody
has triaged them, and inventing 32 rationales would be exactly the fabrication
this repo's honesty rule forbids. The whole baseline expires at once. After
that date every untriaged inherited advisory blocks — either fix it, or move it
into accepted[] with a real reason.
THE UNIT IS THE GHSA ID, NEVER THE PACKAGE. Suppressing 'axios' would silently absorb the next
axios advisory too; suppressing GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9 suppresses exactly one known finding.
KNOWN WORST ITEM IN THE BASELINE: GHSA-3gc7-fjrx-p6mg, a bigint-buffer heap overflow reachable
through @solana/spl-token in an application that signs transactions. npm reports its only fix
as a semver-major downgrade of @solana/spl-token to 0.1.8, which is a product decision and a
code change, not a lockfile bump — that is why it is baselined rather than fixed in the commit
that armed this gate, and why the baseline expiry is 90 days and not a year.

baseline.measuredWith: npm audit --json, npm 10 / node 20, lockfiles as committed on 2026-08-18
